pharm-psych:psymap.e: Mesolimbic D₂ blockade reduces positive symptoms.
No sedation or dependence; takes weeks.

pharm-psych:psymap.q: A 25-year-old woman with schizophrenia has had hallucinations controlled by haloperidol for 3 months. She now has amenorrhea and galactorrhea, and serum prolactin is 85 ng/mL. D₂ blockade in which dopamine pathway explains these findings?
pharm-psych:psymap.e: Dopamine from the tuberoinfundibular tract normally inhibits prolactin release; mesolimbic blockade produces the antipsychotic effect.

pharm-psych:stim.q: A non-stimulant ADHD drug that is a selective NE reuptake inhibitor:

A 9-year-old boy has 1 year of inattention, fidgeting and interrupting others at home and at school, impairing his grades. He is started on first-line drug therapy for this condition. Which adverse effect should be monitored?
pharm-psych:stim.e: ADHD is treated first-line with stimulants (methylphenidate, amphetamines), which suppress appetite and can slow growth; weight gain is typical of atypical antipsychotics.

pharm-psych:antipsych.e: Reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia; also seizures and myocarditis.
Treat with dantrolene or bromocriptine; stop the drug. Autonomic instability and altered mental status are also typical.

pharm-psych:antipsych.q: A 24-year-old man started haloperidol 3 days ago for acute psychosis. He now has painful sustained twisting of his neck to one side and his eyes are fixed upward. What is the most appropriate treatment?
pharm-psych:antipsych.e: Acute dystonia from D₂ blockade responds to anticholinergics (benztropine or diphenhydramine); dantrolene is for neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

pharm-psych:lithium.q: Lithium's narrow therapeutic index is worsened by:

A 40-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder treated for 5 years with lithium passes 5 L of urine daily. Urine osmolality is 150 mOsm/kg and does not rise after desmopressin. What is the mechanism of her polyuria?
o: ↓ ADH response in the collecting duct
pharm-psych:lithium.e: Lithium causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus by impairing ADH-stimulated aquaporin-2 insertion; central DI would respond to desmopressin.

pharm-psych:buspirone.q: Buspirone is useful for generalized anxiety because it:
o: Does not cause sedation or dependence
Acts within hours of the first dose

pharm-psych:buspirone.q: Short-term relief of acute anxiety is best achieved with:
pharm-psych:buspirone.e: Risk of dependence; avoid long term.

pharm-psych:buspirone.q: A 45-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder and a history of alcohol use disorder is started on buspirone. Which counseling point is most important?
o: Taper slowly to avoid withdrawal seizures
Take it only during panic episodes
pharm-psych:buspirone.e: Buspirone (5-HT₁A partial agonist) has delayed onset and no dependence or sedation; withdrawal seizures are a benzodiazepine risk.

pharm-psych:ssri.q: Which SSRI has the longest half-life?
Duloxetine and venlafaxine are SNRIs that can also treat:

A 78-year-old woman started citalopram 3 weeks ago for depression. She is now confused. Serum Na⁺ is 124 mEq/L, she appears euvolemic, and urine osmolality is 450 mOsm/kg. What is the most likely cause of her hyponatremia?
pharm-psych:ssri.e: SSRIs can cause SIADH, especially in older adults, giving euvolemic hyponatremia with inappropriately concentrated urine; primary polydipsia produces dilute urine.

pharm-psych:tca.q: TCAs are avoided in elderly patients mainly because of:
pharm-psych:tca.e: Also sedation and falls; nortriptyline has fewer anticholinergic effects.

pharm-psych:tca.q: Which TCA is used for enuresis?

A 72-year-old man started amitriptyline for postherpetic neuralgia. He now has urinary retention, constipation and dizziness on standing, with BP falling from 130/80 to 100/60 mm Hg. Which receptor blockade explains the orthostatic hypotension?
pharm-psych:tca.e: TCAs block α₁ receptors (orthostasis), muscarinic receptors (retention, constipation) and H₁ receptors (sedation).

pharm-psych:maoi.q: Selegiline at low doses is selective for:

A 50-year-old man treated with phenelzine for depression eats aged cheese and drinks red wine at a party. One hour later he has a severe occipital headache and BP 220/125 mm Hg. What is the mechanism?
pharm-psych:maoi.e: With MAO-A inhibited, dietary tyramine is not degraded and releases norepinephrine from nerve terminals, causing a hypertensive crisis; serotonin syndrome presents with clonus and hyperthermia.

pharm-psych:atypicalad.e: α₂ antagonist; useful in elderly with poor appetite.

pharm-psych:atypicalad.q: A 22-year-old woman with depression also binges and induces vomiting several times a week. She asks for an antidepressant that would also help her quit smoking. Which antidepressant is contraindicated for her?
pharm-psych:atypicalad.e: Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in bulimia and anorexia; fluoxetine is actually approved for bulimia.

pharm-psych:sud.q: Varenicline helps smoking cessation as a:
Naltrexone treats alcohol and opioid use disorder as a:
pharm-psych:sud.e: Disulfiram inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase; acamprosate modulates NMDA.

pharm-psych:sud.q: A 45-year-old man with alcohol use disorder wants medication to reduce drinking. He also takes oxycodone daily for chronic back pain. Which drug should be avoided?
pharm-psych:sud.e: Naltrexone is a μ-opioid antagonist and would precipitate opioid withdrawal and block analgesia; acamprosate is a safe alternative.

pharm-psych:psyrx.q: Drug of choice for acute mania with psychosis:
pharm-psych:psyrx.e: Mood stabilizer = lithium or valproate; mood stabilizers prevent relapse.

pharm-psych:psyrx.q: A 26-year-old woman has recurrent sudden episodes of palpitations, chest tightness and fear of dying that peak within 10 minutes. She now avoids shopping malls, and cardiac evaluation is normal. Which drug is first-line for long-term treatment?
pharm-psych:psyrx.e: Panic disorder is treated long term with an SSRI (plus CBT); benzodiazepines help only briefly because of dependence.

boss.case: A 34-year-old woman has 2 months of low mood, anhedonia, early waking, poor appetite and difficulty concentrating. No psychotic features, no history of mania. She wants to avoid weight gain and sexual side effects if possible.

qs.e: Best tolerability and safety in overdose.

qs.q: How long before an antidepressant's full mood effect?
Which antidepressant has the least sexual dysfunction and no weight gain?
qs.e: NE/DA reuptake inhibitor; lowers seizure threshold.

qs.q: Before starting an antidepressant, screen for bipolar disorder because:
o: SSRIs lower the seizure threshold markedly
Bipolar patients need higher SSRI doses

qs.q: Serotonin syndrome may occur if an SSRI is combined with:
qs.e: Hyperthermia, clonus, agitation; cyproheptadine treats it. Triptans, St John’s wort and other serotonergic drugs also add risk.
